name: The Delhi Sultanate
title: Social Hierarchy of the Delhi Sultanate: From Sultan to Enslaved
in: the Delhi Sultanate under the Tughluqs

tiers.name: The sultan
tiers.you: You rule from Delhi over most of the subcontinent and can order your whole Muslim elite to move to a new capital in the Deccan, but province after province rises against you.
tiers.kid: The sultan of Delhi ruled much of India. One sultan even made his whole court move to a new capital far to the south.
tiers.rise: No fixed rule decided the succession. Ghiyath al-Din seized the throne in 1320, and some historians, among them Vincent Smith, hold that his son killed him in 1325; after Firuz Shah’s death the nobles and his slave guard made and unmade sultans.
tiers.why: The sultan granted and confirmed the iqtas that paid his nobles, and for many Muslim observers his rule was justified by the protection and advancement of the faith.

tiers.name: Nobles and revenue holders
tiers.you: You hold the revenue of a district the sultan has assigned to you, pay your horsemen from it and send the rest to Delhi; under Firuz Shah your son may inherit it.
tiers.kid: Nobles called khans and maliks collected the taxes of lands the sultan gave them and used the money to pay soldiers.
tiers.rise: Office and revenue came from the sultan, and in theory an iqta was not inherited until Firuz Shah made it so. Birth still counted: when the frontier commanders Jalaluddin Khalji and Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq reached for the throne, they found little support because of their un-noble origins.
tiers.why: The great men of the sultanate bore the titles khan and malik, and the elite of its early years were overwhelmingly immigrants from Iran and Central Asia: Persians, Turks, Ghuris and Khalaj.

tiers.name: The sultan's slaves
tiers.you: You were enslaved, made a Muslim and taught the Quran, and now serve in the sultan’s guard, whose leaders will one day put a sultan of their choosing on the throne.
tiers.kid: Some enslaved boys were trained to be soldiers and officials for the sultan, and his slave guard became very powerful.
tiers.rise: Men entered the corps by capture or purchase. Their service could carry them far: after Firuz Shah’s death his old slaves turned against Sultan Abu Bakr Shah and had Nasir ud-Din Muhammad Shah placed on the throne, and under the Khaljis the slave general Malik Kafur, born to a Hindu family, had held power himself in 1316.
tiers.why: Slaves in the sultan’s service could stand above most free people.

tiers.name: Muslim scholars, judges and Sufis
tiers.you: You teach Hanafi law or keep a Sufi lodge, and when the sultan orders the learned to settle in the Deccan you must go with them, to win converts there.
tiers.kid: Muslim scholars and judges taught and used Islamic law, and Sufi holy men were honoured with great tombs.
tiers.rise: Learning and descent made a scholar: sayyids claimed descent from the Prophet Muhammad. The sultan’s favour decided the rest, and Firuz Shah would not tolerate preachers of sects he held to be deviant.
tiers.why: The sultanate followed the Hanafi school of Islamic law, and its judges and learned men wore ample gowns and an Arabic robe, the durra, unlike the soldiers and clerks, who wore the qaba coat.

tiers.name: Hindu chiefs and village officials
tiers.you: You are a Hindu chief who has submitted to the sultan: you keep your own armed men and see the land revenue of your villages collected, as long as you stay loyal and the sultan’s armies stay strong.
tiers.kid: Hindu chiefs and village officials collected taxes for the sultan, but some chiefs rebelled and made their own kingdoms.
tiers.rise: A chief kept his rank by submitting and paying, and lost it by defeat; a rising, as in the south in the 1330s, could make him independent again.
tiers.why: The sultanate claimed to be the paramount power rather than the only one, as earlier Hindu kingdoms had done.

tiers.name: Brahmins and temple priests
tiers.you: You were born a Brahmin and serve in a temple; under Firuz Shah you must pay the jizya, from which your forefathers were free.
tiers.kid: Brahmins were Hindu priests. When soldiers attacked one great temple, its priests hid its holy books and carried its statue away.
tiers.rise: Brahmin rank came by birth. A Brahmin who became a Muslim was freed of the jizya and, under Firuz Shah, given presents and honours.
tiers.why: The Brahmins held a standing that even the sultans recognised: Firuz Shah Tughluq’s predecessor had exempted all Brahmins from the jizya, and Firuz Shah extended the tax to them only at a reduced rate.

tiers.name: Soldiers of the standing army
tiers.you: You ride in the sultan’s cavalry in a qaba coat and red boots, and under Firuz Shah you live on the revenue of a village assigned to you instead of a salary.
tiers.kid: The sultan’s army had hundreds of thousands of horsemen and fought off invaders from Central Asia.
tiers.rise: Horsemen were recruited and bought: the core of the cavalry came from slave backgrounds. Under Firuz Shah a soldier’s village assignment passed to his heirs.
tiers.why: The sultans kept a large standing army.

tiers.name: Townspeople
tiers.you: You work at a craft or trade in Delhi, and when the sultan’s new coins of base metal come in, your neighbours start making their own at home.
tiers.kid: In the towns, craftsmen and traders made and sold goods, and the spinning wheel came into use in India.
tiers.rise: Migrants fleeing the Mongol raids on Central and West Asia brought traders, artists and artisans into the towns. War could also carry artisans away: in 1398 Timur’s army massacred the people of Delhi and took skilled craftsmen to Samarkand as slaves.
tiers.why: The towns held the sultanate’s merchants, craftsmen and labourers.

tiers.name: Peasants
tiers.you: You till your village’s fields and owe the land revenue and the jizya besides; if your village falls behind, the sultan’s men may carry its people off as slaves.
tiers.kid: Most people were farmers who paid heavy taxes on their harvests to the sultan and his nobles.
tiers.rise: Conversion lightened the tax under Firuz Shah, while a village that resisted or failed to pay could be enslaved: Balban had ordered it in Awadh, and Alauddin Khalji made it lawful for revenue defaulters.
tiers.why: The peasants paid for the sultanate.

tiers.name: Enslaved people
tiers.you: You were taken from your village when it fell behind with its taxes, made a Muslim and sold in a town market, where you may be put to building work or sold on to Central Asia.
tiers.kid: Many people were captured in wars or for unpaid taxes and forced to work as slaves, and some were sold far away in Central Asia.
tiers.rise: Some enslaved men rose high in the sultans’ service, as Qutb ud-Din Aibak, a former slave, rose to be the first sultan of Delhi in 1206. Others were carried far from home: in 1398 Timur took men, women and children from Delhi to Samarkand as slaves.
tiers.why: Slavery became the predominant system of North India in the 13th century, André Wink writes, and kept considerable importance in the 14th.
